text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: streaming stalls / decode-tail spike on trt8-us-west-2 pool. Severity: p99 breach. See alert: https://dd.ops/alerts/2102468101

raj: I'm on it. p95 jumped from ~420ms to ~880ms in the last 5m. p99 shot to ~3.6s. Affected routes: /v1/generate (decode-heavy) and streaming websocket lanes.

maria: pulling logs + kernel telemetry. Initial grep shows repeated compilepath warnings from the new kernel set (build id: kset-2026-03-14-417). Errors look like slow kernel fallback on certain shapes.

kai: any recent deploys? I see a trtexec deploy pushed 29m ago (deploy: trt8-upgrade-2026-03-14).

raj: yes, there was a controlled rollout of TRT8 + flash-attn-optimized kernels, flag rollout = "-O3 -fno-rtti -march=sm86" plus AOT compile path enabled. Canary passed but traffic scaled up.

maria: reproducing locally on a smaller mini-batch, I can trigger stalls when sequence_len > 1024 and batch >= 8. KV cache thrash + kernel selection fallback logs look like this:

```
[2026-03-14T15:02:11Z] kernel_selector.cpp: WARN fallback to generic_gemm_kernel for op=decode_attn seq=1536 shape=(8,1536)
[2026-03-14T15:02:11Z] aten_runtime: INFO kernel_compile_time=512ms kernel_link_time=220ms
[2026-03-14T15:02:12Z] runtime: ERROR stall_detected token_emit_delay=1200ms
```

rai: (typo) sorry, raj: I mean maria.

raj: thanks. Can we triage customer impact? Any live customers experiencing errors or just latency?

jen: so far just latency and streaming stalls; websocket clients see intermittent "chunk delayed" but not 5xx. Support reported one customer with increased real-time jitter, they flagged calls with long contexts.

kai: short-term mitigation idea: force kernel set to previous stable (kset-2026-03-01) for decode pool or pin model routing to older variant. We can also flip off AOT compile-path and fall back to JIT kernels.

maria: I can push a mitigation: set env var USE_LEGACY_KERNELS=1 on the trt8-us-west-2 autoscaling group and restart a small shard to observe. That avoids rollback of the whole deploy.

raj: do it. annotate run in this thread. If it works, escalate to partial rollback across region.

maria: running command now:

```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/decode-trt8 USE_LEGACY_KERNELS=1 --record
kubectl rollout restart deploy/decode-trt8
```

maria: restart started on pod decode-trt8-0. watching logs.

(deploy-bot): rollout of deploy/decode-trt8: 1/3 updated. duration 12s.

maria: initial pod logs show new instance warming with legacy kernels. latency on that shard p95 ~460ms, p99 ~1.1s (improved).

raj: good. can you patch autoscaler to route 20% of traffic to legacy-shard until we verify?

kai: done. routing rule updated: decode-trt8 routing weight legacy=20 current=80 — config id r-2102468150.

jen: monitoring: overall cluster p95 dropped to ~520ms, p99 to ~1.6s. Streaming stalls count down 70% in last 6m. Customer impact looks reduced.

maria: I pulled kernel compile logs across all trt8 pods, looks like a specific kernel variant (flashattn_v2) triggers slow link when shape mismatches. Candidate root cause: the compilepath's LTO/linker job sometimes blocks on NFS when concurrency high; if link stalls >200ms we fallback to slower generic kernel at runtime. That fallback path is expensive and causes tail spikes.

kai: check if NFS.io latency correlates.

maria: yes — mounting host /opt/kernel-cache is backed by a shared NFS volume; iostat shows bursts at 15k iops with avg lat 24ms and spikes >200ms during peak.

raj: two-prong plan: 1) immediate: keep legacy kernels routing and disable AOT/link-time compile on decode pools. 2) medium: move kernel cache to local SSD on hosts or introduce a per-node cache lock to avoid thundering herd. 3) longer-term: change compilepath to async compile + prewarm for common shapes.

maria: implemented step 1 for us-west-2 decode pool: flipped flag COMPILE_AOT=0 and confirmed env var propagated.

jen: apply config change to canary first then prod? You already applied to production shard though. Was canary run?

maria: I applied to a small subset (20% routing) then expanded after observing improvement for 4m — will continue staged expansion.

kai: will open infra ticket to move kernel-cache to local ephemeral SSD and add cache sharding. Ticket: INFRA-5129. Assigning to infra oncall Alex.

raj: I'm going to notify SRE lead and PMs for customer-facing comms. Any need to contact customers yet or wait for full mitigation?

jen: monitor another 20m. If p99 <= 1.8s and stalls remain <10% of peak, hold. If not, we should rollback trt8 deploy fully and open postmortem.

maria: agreed. will keep thread updated.

(deploy-bot): rollback candidate available: trt8-upgrade-2026-03-14 -> can rollback via /deploy rollback trt8-upgrade-2026-03-14

raj: note for postmortem: collect kernel compile times, NFS latency metrics, rollout window, canary criteria, customer support tickets.

kai: temp mitigation success metrics documented: reduced stalls by 70%, p99 improved from 3.6s -> 1.4s cluster-wide, CPU impact on legacy kernel pods +8% (acceptable).

jen: I'll update the incident dashboard and open a high-priority page to PM/customer-ops.

maria: logging snapshots and bundle uploaded: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/2102468101-bundle.tar.gz

raj: thanks team. Oncall handoff in 30m — @kai you'll take next shift; leave any runbooks here.

kai: taking handoff. leaving runbook notes:
- keep legacy routing at 20% until midnight local
- watch streaming_stalls.count and decode.p99
- if stalls climb >30% of baseline rollback trt8 deploy

raj: :thumbsup: handing off to @kai.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to "mitigated (partial)". SLA impact: degraded latency for 42m. Postmortem requested.
